input_references.role: Timestamped trajectory points linked by trajectory_id

metadata.goal: Find same points and differences of three users based on given trajectories within five weekdays.
metadata.category: Three-user riverside-hub periodicity, café repetition, shopping-area coordination, and driving behaviour
metadata.dataset_description: Three users visit a shared riverside-recreation hub on successive weekdays and then follow different driving or shopping routines. Official land-use labels follow the unchanged endpoints; Unmapped denotes an endpoint outside reference polygons.
metadata.metric_note: `mid_trajectory_speed_kmh` is the mean point speed from 20% to 80% trajectory progress; `passes_riverside` denotes a riverside context for motor-vehicle trips. Same-day hub dwell time is derived by subtracting the inbound `arrival_time` from the subsequent outbound `start_time`; all such gaps are between 3.25 and 4.67 hours.
metadata.land_use_reference: Archived PUM2050 Affectatio polygons (2025). Labels describe reference-map zoning at fixed endpoints, not surveyed activities at the time of travel.
metadata.motion_consistency_note: Point speed is the incoming segment GPS great-circle distance divided by elapsed time; the first point repeats the first outgoing segment speed. Earth radius: 6371.0088 km. Trip distance is the sum of these segment distances. avg_speed_kmh and mean_speed_kmh are total distance / elapsed time; avg_point_speed_kmh and point_speed_mean_kmh are unweighted means of the delivered point speeds. speed_cv is the population coefficient of variation of incoming segment speeds, excluding the duplicated first endpoint. trajectory_progress is point_index / (point_count - 1), not elapsed-time fraction. Timestamps and speed fields were reconstructed for internal consistency on 2026-10-09; GPS positions and insight wording were preserved. These are curated example records, not newly recovered observations.

insight_list.insight: Weekday arrival times at the shared riverside-recreation hub differ across users, while remaining relatively consistent for each individual.

insight_list.question: For each user, are arrivals at the same riverside-recreation hub stable across the five weekdays despite differing origins?
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
df = pd.read_csv(dataset_path)
points = pd.read_csv(Path(dataset_path).with_name('trajectory_points.csv'))
hub=df[df.trip_stage.eq('to_shared_hub')]; print(hub.groupby('user_id').arrival_hour.agg(['min','max','mean','std'])); print(hub.destination_land_use.value_counts())
insight_list.evidence: All 15 hub endpoints occupy the same GPS location, mapped as Récréation et accès aux rives. The arrival windows remain distinct across users.

insight_list.insight: After spending several hours at the shared hub, User A follows a fixed driving routine, while Users B and C show more variable public-transit shopping patterns.

insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
df = pd.read_csv(dataset_path)
points = pd.read_csv(Path(dataset_path).with_name('trajectory_points.csv'))
follow=df[df.purpose_group.isin(['cafe','shopping'])]; print(pd.crosstab(follow.user_id,follow.mode_group)); print(follow.groupby(['weekday','destination_id']).user_id.apply(list))
